evidence: Only method 0x0027C2F0 Ui_BattlePopup_Show loads self->f_204, calls its vt[+0x18](1) and vt[+0x74](0) and then Battle_PopupEntry_Create(f204, text, arg4, arg5, numLo, numHi, src); the class name comes from that method, no ctor or vtable was recovered for the class itself.

fields.name: popupManager
fields.evidence: self->f_204 is the first argument of Battle_PopupEntry_Create (0x002DFDE8), which reads its +0x1C4/+0x1C8/+0x1CC entry lists and its +0x24 allocator and allocates the 0x24-byte entry; the same pointer's vt[+0x18]/vt[+0x74] activate and reset it before the create. No structs.json class has those offsets, so the type stays void*.

summary: Choice/confirm prompt state block: counts ticks while the prompt is up and, after 0x27 ticks, hands control back to the input manager; the start/confirm paths also copy the two default words from 0x00728550 into +4/+8.
evidence: Four methods take this object: 0x003EB618 Ui_Choice_SetSelectedIndex (the name source), 0x003EB694 maybe_Ui_Choice_Start, 0x003EB994 maybe_Ui_Choice_Confirm and 0x003EBA30 maybe_Ui_Choice_Tick; the last three still have no callers, so only the widget family is certain.

fields.name: tickCounter
fields.evidence: maybe_Ui_Choice_Tick does iVar1 = self->f_10 + 1; self->f_10 = iVar1 and fires when 0x27 < iVar1; maybe_Ui_Choice_Confirm sets self->f_10 = 0.

summary: Five-digit rolling counter widget: every update advances a step counter and scrolls the five digit sprites, and the update reports completion after 0x2E steps.
evidence: Ctor 0x002D00EC installs vtable 0x00760480 (slot +4 is Ui_DigitRoll_DeletingDtor 0x002D010C) and clears +0x11C; update 0x002CFE5C loops i<5 over func_003942A8(ctx->f_c, i).

fields.name: stepCounter
fields.evidence: Ui_DigitRoll_Update plays SE 0xE61 when f_10==0 and 0xE62 when f_10==10, computes each digit's scroll offset as i*-5 + f_10, then increments f_10 and returns 0x2E < f_10.

summary: Not a real class: struct_db grouped 14 UI functions that all reference the one-time-init guard 0x007BE2D0. Thirteen are identical __cxa_guard_acquire stubs and only 0x0069A028 has a body, which fills a 16-byte record from its arguments.
evidence: 13 of the 14 methods (0x00694B78, 0x00695E30, 0x00699FE0, 0x0069DA98, 0x0069DF30, 0x0069EAE0, 0x0069ED04, 0x0069FEAC, 0x006A147C, 0x006A1EEC, 0x006A2118, 0x006A28CC, 0x006A0CD4) decompile to a single func_0010009C(0x007BE2D0) guard call; only 0x0069A028 writes the object at param_1.

fields.name: unknown_id
fields.evidence: asm 0x0069A028: strh r2,[r0] then str r2,[r0,#4] and stm r4={r2,0xff} at +8/+0xC, i.e. a 16-byte record {u16 id; u32 a; u32 b; u32 0xFF} filled from the caller's arguments. Nothing identifies the id, so it stays unknown.

summary: Equipment-detail panel: shows one item for one party member and applies the item's stat-boost roll; the two recovered methods are the two scroll directions of the detail page.
evidence: Both methods 0x003D6480/0x003D6750 resolve the item through Item_LookupRecord(self->f_8) and the member through func_0035EB98(work, memberId), then push panes on the panel at self->f_4 and call Ui_Panel_ResetAndPush; base Ui_Panel from two base-constructor calls.

fields.name: maybe_textSource
fields.evidence: Both scroll handlers end with *(int *)(*(int *)(self + 4) + 0x10CC) = self + 0x14 followed by Ui_Panel_ResetAndPush(panel), so the panel is handed the address of this field and re-reads it on every push; nothing in the batch writes it, so the payload is unknown.

summary: Stale struct_db grouping: the single method 0x001C69BC is now maybe_Ui_Window_ScriptCommandHandlerM, a UI window action-script command handler, so this object is a Ui_Window (embedded child widgets at +0x804/+0x9D8/+0xF84, a pane table and a script-state byte vector at +0x10A8).
evidence: asm 0x001C69BC: add r1,r4,#0xC00 / add r1,r1,#0x384 = self+0xF84, then Ui_Object_BroadcastToChildren(r1,1); the same handler broadcasts to self+0x804 and self+0x9D8, hides six panes through 0x0029126C and pushes 0x0B into the byte vector at self+0x10A8. The class name is kept only because apply.py matches structs.json.

fields.name: childObject
fields.evidence: Ui_Object_BroadcastToChildren(self + 0xF84, 1) passes the field's address, so this is an embedded Ui_Object sub-widget (the header uses the project's pointer convention for sub-objects); the same handler broadcasts to the embedded objects at +0x804 and +0x9D8.

summary: Stale struct_db grouping: 0x004A3B3C is the Field_InteractJob deleting destructor (type table 0x775558) while 0x004A3C74/0x004A3D14 are message formatters that read a spell/skill id at +0x208, so the three methods do not share one class.
evidence: Field_InteractJob is 72 bytes in structs.json yet the two formatters read self+0x208, so the batch mixes two different objects; the class name is kept only because apply.py matches structs.json.

fields.name: actionId
fields.evidence: Message_FormatArg5FromSpellRecord passes self->f_208 to the SpellRecord accessor 0x0063CFC8 and Message_FormatArg5FromSkillRecord passes the same byte to the SkillRecord accessor 0x0063D018, so it is the id of the action whose description is being formatted into message argument 5.

summary: Scene layout-request block: the four recovered methods build a one-byte layout-kind request and hand it to the matching Ui_Layout_LoadAndBind_TypeN loader; the block also holds the scene's model resource handles.
evidence: 0x002D6B68/0x002D6B80/0x002D6BB0/0x002D6C7C all take the scene pointer, write the kind byte (6/1/4/5) on the stack and tail-call Ui_Layout_LoadAndBind_Type6/1/4/5; callers are Ui_Window_OpenScene and Ui_SceneFlow_AdvanceState.

fields.name: resourceSectionHandles
fields.evidence: Ui_LayoutRequest_Type1 (0x002D6B80) loads the pointer and passes it as the out block to maybe_Ui_LayoutRequest_LoadResourceSections (0x002448BC), which writes four 8-byte pack handle pairs into it (res/model3d.bxon, two more, res/motion/equip.bxon)

summary: Reference to one UI list row: an index plus a kind byte that selects which row table the resolver walks (bag rows, the external list, or the 20-row table).
evidence: Ui_ListItemRef_ResolveRow (0x006308EC) reads *ref as the index and (char)ref[3] as the kind, then returns work+0x24A98+0x5FE4+idx*0x8C (kind 0), *0x007AB814+0x6B8+idx*0x98 (kind 1) or work+0x24A98+0x7B3C+idx*0x8C (kind 2).

fields.name: kind
fields.evidence: cVar1 = (char)ref[3] selects the row table: 0 = bag rows, 1 = external list, 2 = the 20-row table; the sibling 0x00630998 is the same resolver without the kind-1 branch. Only the low byte of the word at +0xC is used.
